pharm: Intravenous ACE inhibitor (the active de-esterified metabolite of enalapril) that blocks conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, lowering blood pressure by reducing vasoconstriction and aldosterone-driven sodium/water retention.

Given intravenously; not related to meals

summary: Enalaprilat is the active intravenous angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor form of enalapril, used for the treatment of hypertension when oral therapy is not practical. The usual dose is 1.25 mg IV every 6 hours given over about 5 minutes; in patients on diuretics or with renal impairment (CrCl <=30 mL/min) the starting dose is reduced to 0.625 mg. It lowers blood pressure by inhibiting ACE, decreasing angiotensin II and aldosterone. It carries a BOXED WARNING for fetal toxicity - drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus, especially in the second and third trimesters, and must be discontinued as soon as pregnancy is detected. Key risks include symptomatic hypotension (especially in volume- or salt-depleted patients), angioedema (which can be life-threatening and is more common in Black patients), hyperkalemia, renal impairment, and rare agranulocytosis and hepatic injury.
indications: Treatment of hypertension when oral therapy is not practical (hospitalized adults)

dosage.d: 1.25 mg IV every 6 hours, administered over 5 minutes
dosage.n: Doses up to 5 mg per dose have been tolerated for up to 36 hours

dosage.d: Initial 0.625 mg IV over 5 minutes; if inadequate response after 1 hour, may repeat 0.625 mg and continue 1.25 mg every 6 hours thereafter
dosage.n: Observe at least 1 hour after first dose for hypotension

dosage.c: Renal impairment (CrCl <=30 mL/min) or serum creatinine >3 mg/dL
dosage.d: Initial 0.625 mg IV; if inadequate response after 1 hour, repeat 0.625 mg and give 1.25 mg every 6 hours thereafter

dosage.c: Conversion from IV to oral enalapril
dosage.d: If IV 1.25 mg q6h was effective, start oral enalapril 5 mg once daily (2.5 mg once daily if on diuretic or with renal impairment), adjusting per response
dosage.n: Transition when oral therapy becomes practical

admin: Administer as a slow intravenous injection over at least 5 minutes, or diluted in up to 50 mL of compatible IV solution
Monitor blood pressure closely during and after the dose, especially after the first dose
Reduce or correct volume/salt depletion before starting where possible; have IV normal saline available for hypotension
Use reduced 0.625 mg starting dose in diuretic-treated patients and in renal impairment
Stop the drug and treat promptly if angioedema or severe hypotension occurs
moa: Enalaprilat competitively inhibits angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE, kininase II), preventing the conversion of angiotensin I to the potent vasoconstrictor angiotensin II. The fall in angiotensin II reduces vasoconstriction and decreases aldosterone secretion, lowering sodium and water retention and reducing blood pressure. Decreased angiotensin II also reduces negative feedback on renin, raising plasma renin activity. Inhibition of kininase II additionally reduces breakdown of bradykinin, which may contribute to vasodilation and to side effects such as cough and angioedema. Enalaprilat is the active de-esterified moiety; enalapril is its oral prodrug.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to enalaprilat/enalapril or any component
History of angioedema related to previous ACE inhibitor therapy
Concomitant use with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril); do not give within 36 hours of switching
Concomitant use of aliskiren in patients with diabetes mellitus
relative: Volume- or salt-depleted patients (heart failure, high-dose diuretics, dialysis) - risk of severe first-dose hypotension
Bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis in a solitary kidney
Collagen vascular disease with renal involvement (neutropenia/agranulocytosis risk)
monitor: Blood pressure for symptomatic hypotension, especially after the first dose
Signs of angioedema (face, lips, tongue, larynx, intestine) and white blood cell count in at-risk patients

preg: BOXED WARNING: Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and even death to the developing fetus when used in the second and third trimesters; fetal toxicity includes oligohydramnios, renal failure, hypotension, skull hypoplasia and death. When pregnancy is detected, discontinue enalaprilat as soon as possible.
lact: Enalapril and enalaprilat are detected in human breast milk in small amounts. Because of the potential for adverse effects, a decision should be made whether to discontinue breastfeeding or the drug; avoid in mothers of newborns and premature infants if alternatives exist.
renal: Reduce the starting dose to 0.625 mg IV in patients with creatinine clearance <=30 mL/min (or serum creatinine >3 mg/dL) and titrate cautiously. Monitor renal function and potassium closely; enalaprilat is removed by hemodialysis.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is needed for hepatic impairment because enalaprilat is the active compound and, unlike oral enalapril, does not require hepatic conversion. Rare cholestatic hepatitis/hepatic failure has been reported with ACE inhibitors - discontinue if marked liver enzyme elevation or jaundice occurs.

major: Aliskiren (in diabetes) and dual RAAS blockade with ARBs - increased hypotension, hyperkalemia and renal impairment; avoid
Neprilysin inhibitors (sacubitril) - increased angioedema risk; contraindicated/observe 36-hour washout
Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes - risk of severe hyperkalemia
moderate: NSAIDs (including selective COX-2 inhibitors) - may blunt antihypertensive effect and worsen renal function/hyperkalemia, especially in the elderly or volume-depleted
Diuretics - augmented blood pressure lowering and first-dose hypotension
Lithium - reduced lithium clearance with risk of lithium toxicity
mTOR inhibitors / DPP-4 inhibitors (e.g., sirolimus, sitagliptin) - increased angioedema risk
minor: Antidiabetic agents - possible enhanced hypoglycemic effect
Other antihypertensives - additive blood pressure lowering
interactions.food: Not applicable for intravenous use; avoid high-potassium salt substitutes.
interactions.alcohol: Alcohol may enhance the blood-pressure-lowering effect; advise caution.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum potassium and renal function; may cause false-low aldosterone and altered renin measurements.

serious: Angioedema of the face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis and/or larynx (potentially fatal airway obstruction)
rare: Agranulocytosis / neutropenia (especially with renal impairment or collagen vascular disease)
Anaphylactoid reactions (e.g., during hemodialysis with high-flux membranes or LDL apheresis)
Intestinal angioedema presenting as abdominal pain

monitoring: Blood pressure during and after each dose, particularly the first dose and in volume-depleted patients
Serum creatinine and BUN for renal function
Observation for angioedema (face, lips, tongue, larynx, abdominal)
White blood cell count in patients with renal impairment or collagen vascular disease
counsel: This is an intravenous blood-pressure medicine given and monitored in the hospital; you may feel lightheaded - tell the team if you feel faint
Report immediately any swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing or swallowing (signs of angioedema)
If you are or may become pregnant, tell your doctor at once - this drug can harm an unborn baby and must be stopped
Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes unless your doctor approves; your potassium and kidney function will be checked
Report persistent dizziness, reduced urination, yellowing of the skin/eyes, or signs of infection (fever, sore throat)
pk: Blood pressure reduction within about 15 minutes of IV dosing
About 6 hours at recommended doses (basis for q6h dosing)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F) [USP controlled room temperature]
pearls: BOXED WARNING: fetal toxicity - discontinue as soon as pregnancy is detected
IV ACE inhibitor used when oral therapy is impractical; standard dose 1.25 mg q6h, reduce to 0.625 mg if diuretic-treated or CrCl <=30 mL/min
Watch for first-dose hypotension in volume-/salt-depleted patients; have IV saline ready
Angioedema can be life-threatening and is more common in Black patients; ACE-inhibitor angioedema is a contraindication to future use
Avoid combination with aliskiren in diabetics and with sacubitril (neprilysin inhibitor); monitor potassium and renal function
missed: Enalaprilat is given on a fixed in-hospital schedule (typically every 6 hours) by the care team; there is no patient-managed missed dose. If a scheduled dose is delayed, the team gives it when appropriate and resumes the every-6-hour interval, with blood pressure monitoring.
overdose: The most likely manifestation of overdose is marked hypotension. Treatment is with intravenous normal saline infusion to restore blood pressure; place the patient supine. Monitor and correct electrolytes (hyperkalemia) and renal function. Enalaprilat is removed by hemodialysis, which may be used in severe cases; angiotensin II infusion or catecholamines may be considered for refractory hypotension.
